title: Finite Tor amplitude descends from a finite principal localization cover
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules (modules $K^n$ and $R$-linear maps $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ with $d^{n+1}d^n=0$) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $a\le b$ be integers. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, with $r\ge0$, generate the unit ideal, and write $R_{f_i}=R[1/f_i]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Use the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], specialized to the site with one object, only its identity morphism, and only the maximal covering sieve, so that sheaves of rings and modules are rings and modules. Derived tensor with an arbitrary module, placed in degree zero, is the ordinary-module derived tensor product computed on K-flat models by [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. If, for every $i$, the localized complex $K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ (meaning that $H^n((K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i})\otimes_{R_{f_i}}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R_{f_i}$-module $N$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$), then $K^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: $H^n(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: Fix an R-module M. Use the already proved ordinary-module theorem CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism π:P→K with P categorically K-flat. The single-degree specialization QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso of [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] identifies K tensor-derived M[0] with Q(C), where C is termwise P tensor M.

proof.text: For each i put S=R[1/f_i] and F=ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap R S). Localization is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Mathlib ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat supplies the exact scalar-extension functor (the categorical form of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]); it preserves homology and quasi-isomorphisms. Thus F(π) gives Q(F(P))≅Q(F(K)).

proof.text: Convert categorical K-flatness to preservation of acyclic tensor products on the homotopy quotient, apply [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars], and convert back using the braiding for the other tensor factor. This proves F(P) K-flat. The monoidal scalar-extension comparison Functor.Monoidal.commTensorRight, lifted by NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex, gives F(C)≅F(P) tensor F(M) termwise. QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] and Q(F(π)) now identify Q(F(C)) with Q(F(K)) tensor-derived F(M)[0]. Apply the assumed local Tor amplitude to F(M) and transport both cohomological bounds along this isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 066N, proof of lemma-glue-tor-amplitude; explicit K-flat computation of the displayed localization identity

proof.text: For every n<a or b<n, local cohomological concentration gives zero degree-n homology of every F(C). Apply [lem-pc-homology-vanishing-localization-span] with the original unit-ideal hypothesis to deduce vanishing of degree-n homology of C. DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff give concentration of Q(C) in [a,b]. Transport along the global tensor-model isomorphism of step 1 and vary M. The localization-span criterion includes an empty cover and the zero ring. No boundedness or flatness of M is imposed.
